task:
Adversarially review your own prior annotation. The full brief is `TASK.md` in your working directory — READ IT FIRST and follow it. This block restates only what is easiest to skip.
Your prior artifact is `input/oracle.json`. It is yours. You have never seen another annotator's output and you will not see one now. Everything else you may read is under `bundle/`; read `bundle/docs/assurance/evidence/measurement/measurement-contract.md` — it is the specification, TASK.md is not.
Produce: out/oracle.json the revised, re-sealed artifact out/REVIEW.md what you attacked, what changed, what survived
THE POINT OF THIS PASS: an interpretive judgment that felt obvious is the kind a second reader with the same habits would also accept, and agreement produced that way is not evidence of correctness. For each in-scope row, write the STRONGEST case that your own disposition is wrong, then decide on the bytes whether that case defeats it. "My first reading was reasonable" is not a defence. `ambiguous` is a legitimate destination when the attack shows the prose never chose.
THE RULE THAT STILL MATTERS MOST: do not write a program that decides. Contract §4.4 binds this pass exactly as it bound the first. Tooling may locate rows, compute offsets, verify spans and assemble JSON. It may not decide whether a sentence makes a claim or which occurrence it binds to.
The domain does not change: same anchors, exactly one row each, no additions or removals. Re-seal the artifact and recompute its digest.
Node 24 is available. No network, no dependencies.
structured_output_contract: Report at the end: 1. Rows in scope, rows changed, broken out by transition. 2. Every changed row: anchor identity, old and new disposition, the attack that succeeded, and the corpus words that decided it. 3. Rows attacked that survived: how many, and the hardest few with the attack you made and why the text defeated it. 4. Any `lexical:` row you corrected. 5. What you would still want a human to decide. 6. Anything you read outside `bundle/`.
grounding_rules: Every changed row must name the words in the corpus that defeated the original reading, not a pattern that matched. Cite the contract clause for anything the contract governs. A low change count is a finding if the attacks genuinely failed; do not manufacture changes, and do not protect the first pass either.
